title: Universal fixed-rank locus inside the bounded-generator open
statement: Let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme (quasi-compact and locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]), let $F$ be a coherent $\mathcal O_S$-module [pqf-def-coherent], and let $r\geq0$. Write $\kappa(s)$ for the residue field [def-weil-residue-field]. The subset $W_r(F)=\{s\in S:\dim_{\kappa(s)}(F_s\otimes_{\mathcal O_{S,s}}\kappa(s))\leq r\}$ is open. There is a quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I_r\subseteq\mathcal O_{W_r(F)}$ and a closed immersion $C_r(F)\hookrightarrow W_r(F)$ [def-weil-closed-immersion] cut out by $\mathcal I_r$, such that for every scheme $T$ and every $g:T\to S$, $g^*F$ [def-pc-module-pullback] is locally free of rank $r$ if and only if $g$ factors uniquely through $C_r(F)\to S$. Here locally free of rank $r$ means locally isomorphic to $\mathcal O_T^{\oplus r}$. Both $W_r(F)\to S$ and $C_r(F)\to S$ are of finite presentation (locally of finite presentation, quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]). In particular, when all fibre dimensions are at most $r$, $C_r(F)$ is closed in $S$.

source.place: Tag 05P8, lemma-locally-free-rank-r-pullback, parts (2),(3) and final finite-presentation assertion; Tag 0C3F, lemma-fitting-ideal-generate-locally, and more-algebra.tex Tag 07ZC identify the bounded-generator open with the fibre-dimension bound. This is the coherent case of Bourbaki Expose 221 Lemma 3.6.

proof.text: By [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth], $F$ is quasi-coherent of finite type. Its stalk at any $s$ is finite: take the germs of finitely many local generators. Nakayama [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators] says that the stalk is generated by at most $r$ elements exactly when its residue vector space has dimension at most $r$: lift a residue basis and pad with zeros; conversely images of $r$ generators span the residue space. By clause (2) of [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-generate-locally], these conditions are equivalent to $s\notin|Z_r|$, where $Z_r$ is cut out by $\operatorname{Fit}_r(F)$. Thus $W=W_r(F)=S\setminus|Z_r|$ is open, and $F|_W$ is locally generated by at most $r$ sections.

On $W$, take $\mathcal I=\operatorname{Fit}_{r-1}(F|_W)$ for $r>0$ and $\mathcal I=0$ for $r=0$. By [def-trf-fitting-ideal-sheaf] restriction uses the same affine ideal family. By [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-ideal-closed-subscheme] it cuts out $i:C\hookrightarrow W$, with charts $\operatorname{Spec}(A/\mathcal I(U))$. For $r=0$, $F|_W=0$ and $C=W$.

This is the coherent case of Bourbaki Expose 221 Lemma 3.6.

proof.text: For $h:T\to W$, apply [lem-sfb-bounded-generators-fitting-pullback-criterion] to $E=F|_W$: $h^*E$ is locally free of rank $r$ exactly when $h^*\mathcal I\to\mathcal O_T$ vanishes. Its affine tensor description uses the same ring map $A\to B$ for $h^*E$ and $(jh)^*F$.

source.place: Tag 05P8, lemma-locally-free-rank-r-pullback, parts (2),(3) and final finite-presentation assertion; Tag 0C3F, lemma-fitting-ideal-generate-locally, and more-algebra.tex Tag 07ZC identify the bounded-generator open with the fibre-dimension bound. This is the coherent case of Bourbaki Expose 221 Lemma 3.6.

proof.text: If $g^*F$ is locally free of rank $r$, [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-generate-locally](1) factors $g=jh$ through $W$. Step 3 says that all ideal sections die on an affine cover, hence on $h^{-1}(U)$ by the sheaf axiom. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-lift-ideal-kills-sections] to lift $h$ through $C$. Conversely a lift kills $\mathcal I$ by the quotient charts of Step 2, so Step 3 proves local freeness.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-noetherian-open-closed-finite-presentation] to $i,j$: $W$ is locally Noetherian and $j,i,ji$ are monomorphisms and of finite presentation in the full LFP/QC/QS sense. Thus the factorization in Step 4 is unique and both required morphisms are finitely presented. If all fibre dimensions are at most $r$, then $W=S$ and $C\hookrightarrow W$ is closed in $S$.
